title: Responding to Mass Shootings: How Victims, Shooters, and Elected Officials Shape Congressional Statements
abstract: Mass shootings play an outsize role in United States gun policy debates. But mass shootings vary in their social impact. This paper considers why some mass shootings resonate, while others quickly fade from memory. It examines one set of actors—elected government officials—who help elevate mass shootings in the public agenda. Using data on press releases, mass shootings, and members of the US House of Representatives over 4 years, regression analyses reveal that representatives’ responses to mass shootings are a function of the victims, the shooters, and the officials themselves. Party differences are apparent, with Republicans and Democrats responding differently to electoral incentives. The research helps us to understand why some mass shootings resonate and persist in collective memory.
